focus: Derived metadata refresh and continuity saves
answeredQuestions: Which derived-metadata refreshes after a doc edit (description.json, graph-metadata.json fingerprints, continuity saves) are mandatory, and which are pure overhead per edit?

keyFindings.text: Each packet carries two derived documents that are recomputed from its prose: `graph-metadata.json` holds 17 derived fields including `trigger_phrases`, `key_topics`, `source_fingerprint`, `source_doc_hashes`, `causal_summary` and `save_lineage`, and `description.json` holds derived keywords, level and a `lastUpdated` stamp, so any wording edit invalidates them by design. [SOURCE: specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/011-authoring-speed-research/graph-metadata.json:1] [SOURCE: specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/011-authoring-speed-research/description.json:1]

Derived-file and continuity rules are the largest single rule family: 16 of the 41 validator rules judge a description, a graph, a fingerprint or a continuity block rather than authored content. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/lib/validator-registry.json:1]

Strict mode turns that upkeep into a hard failure: `GENERATED_METADATA_DRIFT` is strict-only at error severity and re-derives the folder before comparing, so a wording edit can fail a strict check on metadata alone even when every sentence in the packet is correct. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/lib/validator-registry.json:1]

The refresh already belongs to the save, not to each edit: every planner mode of `generate-context.js` refreshes `description.json`, `graph-metadata.json` and the phase-parent pointers, and only `--full-auto` writes the continuity fields, so a per-edit metadata refresh duplicates work the save performs anyway. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/memory/save-workflow.md:257]

The authoring card pushes that refresh outside the author's window: its forbidden list names `generate-context.js` and `/speckit:save`, so the derived refresh and the continuity write happen after the authoring worker stops, at the exact moment nobody is reading the diff the refresh produces. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/workflows/spec-authoring-card.md:25]

The continuity fingerprint is self-invalidating by construction: `CONTINUITY_FRESHNESS` recomputes a SHA-256 over `implementation-summary.md`'s own text with the fingerprint line zeroed and also requires packet paths clean, so every later edit to that document makes the stored value stale, and the rule is inert unless `SPECKIT_COMPLETION_FRESHNESS=true`. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/validation/validation-rules.md:150]

The wall-clock stamps guarantee a diff on every save: `lastUpdated` in `description.json` and `last_save_at` plus `last_accessed_at` and `last_active_at` in the graph's derived block change on each save even when no prose changed, which costs reviewers a noisy diff and parallel workers a merge point for zero content information. [SOURCE: specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/011-authoring-speed-research/description.json:8]

The structural repair loop has no changed-only mode: `repair-derived.cjs` is dry by default and prints an apply command, but the documented flow names one `--folder` per changed packet and then a separate track-root refresh, so repair cost scales with every packet a move touches rather than with the packets whose prose changed. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/repair-derived.cjs:16] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/structure/phase-definitions.md:96]

The shared track index makes every new packet an edit to a shared file: `specs/system-speckit/graph-metadata.json` carries 20 `children_ids` in 2,890 bytes and `create.sh` appends the new packet to it, so parallel packet work converges on one small file again and again. [SOURCE: specs/system-speckit/graph-metadata.json:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/workflows/spec-authoring-card.md:49]
